subject: Recap & compatibility checklist — FastHealth LLM migration
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Recap & compatibility checklist — FastHealth LLM migration

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick write-up to capture what we heard and proposed next steps so everyone has the same frame. If I missed anything, please flag.

Key pain points you shared
- Heavy reliance on a single proprietary API (OpenAI) with cost and throttling surprises at scale
- Need deterministic latency for clinical triage flows (90th pctile < 300ms)
- Data governance: PII concerns and auditability for model inputs/outputs
- Tight integration with an internal prompt orchestration layer and embedding index (we heard: Elasticsearch-backed vector store)

Current stack (as described)
- Chat: OpenAI gpt-4o via HTTP API, ~120M tokens/month
- Embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small for semantic search (index in Elasticsearch)
- Orchestration: Homegrown prompt service routes calls, performs template substitution, and stores traces in Postgres
- SLOs: sub-300ms p95 for low-latency routes, nightly batch summarization ok with higher latency

Success criteria for migration to open models
- Functional parity for prompts and embedding workflows (same tokenization behavior where possible)
- Meet latency targets for the triage route (p95 < 300ms) and cost reduction target: 25%–40% per embedding/query unit
- End-to-end observability and audit logs comparable to current traces
- Graduation plan (pilot -> prod) with a rollback path to current API

Compatibility notes / preliminary asks from our side
- Request: export of your current prompt templates and a small representative prompt set (5–10 examples) so we can validate model parity
- Request: sample API call patterns (RPS, token distributions) — we can use an anonymized CSV (example column layout: route, method, tokens_in, tokens_out, timestamp)
- Confirm: embeddings schema (dims) and whether you can accept 1536-d vectors (or require 3072+)

Attachments included in this email
- fasthealth_api_inventory.csv (template we can use for your API call patterns)

Proposed next steps
1) You share the inventory + prompt set (target: by Tue 8/31)
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/eng (1 hour) — proposed slots: Wed 9/1 10:00am PT or Thu 9/2 2:00pm PT
3) We’ll produce a compatibility matrix and cost/latency sketch for the pilot within 5 business days of receiving artifacts

If that all sounds right I’ll lock in the deep-dive and drop the compatibility matrix into the Drive link above.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Thanks Neha — this looks good and aligns with our notes. A couple of clarifications and additions from our side: 

Clarifications
- Embeddings: current vector dim is 1536 (we can move to 3072 but would prefer to avoid unless necessary)
- Monthly token usage: ~120M input tokens, ~30M output tokens (mostly chat-heavy during business hours)
- Sensitive data: PHI sometimes appears in free-text triage notes — we need a model routing policy and KMS integration for keys at-rest

What we’ll share this week
- Prompt set: 8 representative prompts (triage, discharge summary compression, clinical Q&A)
- Inventory CSV: we’ll populate your template and send by Mon 8/31 EOD
- Security questionnaire: I’ll attach a redacted SOC2 extract for our security team to compare

One ask: on the compatibility matrix, please call out any known tokenization differences between OpenAI models and the open models you’ll recommend, and how that might affect prompt framing. Also flag any embed dimension mismatch implications for our ES index.

We’re OK with the Wed 9/1 10am PT slot for the technical deep-dive — Tom (CTO) will join.

Thanks,
Aisha Gupta
